# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**RE:** Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-14
**Member:** Quinn Iverson
**Member ID:** W154693844
**Reference number:** POC-E14E3A00BC-47205
**Plan:** Wellpoint (Commercial/ACA), New Jersey
**Governing policy:** *Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery* (Carelon), https://files.providernews.anthem.com/2519/PDF-Small-Joint-Surgery-2023-11-05.pdf (effective 11/05/2023)

Dear Wellpoint Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702). My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the records already in your file meet the plan's own published criteria for this surgery. I am asking that this decision be reconsidered.

## Why I believe the denial should be reversed

The denial letter states that "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I understand the plan's own guideline sets out the specific criteria for ankle arthroplasty, and I want to walk through each one against my records.

**1. Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint**

The guideline states that ankle arthroplasty is medically necessary when there is:

> "Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint"

My weight-bearing ankle radiographs, taken 2026-07-17, showed tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts. This is documented in my imaging report.

**2. Significant pain and functional impairment persisting after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management**

The guideline requires:

> "Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management"

My records show 18 months of progressive ankle pain, unrelieved by rest. I completed 16 weeks (20 visits) of supervised physical therapy from 2026-03-24 to 2026-07-14, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also took NSAIDs for 4 months without adequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-05 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. This is well beyond the 3-month period the plan's own criteria describe. As for functional impairment, the guideline defines it this way:

> "For the purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes."

My records document that I ambulate with an antalgic gait and am limited to walking two blocks, with positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion on exam. [If a numeric VAS pain score was recorded in the chart, I ask that it be added to this appeal record to confirm it meets or exceeds the ≥4 threshold.]

**3. Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion**

The guideline also requires:

> "Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses)"

[Please refer to the vascular examination findings in my chart, or I will ask Dr. Okafor's office to submit a supplemental note confirming pedal pulse status, to address this element directly.]

**4. FDA-approved device**

The guideline states the "Device is FDA approved" as a requirement. [Dr. Okafor's office can confirm the specific device to be used and its FDA approval status if this has not already been provided.]

Taken together, my records show progressive, disabling ankle arthritis confirmed on imaging, and a conservative treatment course — physical therapy, NSAIDs, and corticosteroid injection — that lasted well beyond the 3-month period referenced in the plan's own guideline. I do not believe the record supports a finding that conservative treatment was inadequate or too brief.

## What I am asking for

I am asking Wellpoint to reconsider this denial in light of the clinical records already submitted and this appeal, and to approve the requested total ankle replacement (CPT 27702). If any additional documentation — such as the vascular exam findings or device information noted above — would help complete this review, please let me know what is needed and I will work with Dr. Okafor's office to provide it.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-10. Please send your response to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, or I can be reached using the contact information below.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

________________________
Quinn Iverson
Member ID: W154693844
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [date of submission]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

evidence.policy_title: Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon)
quotes: ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met:

• Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint • Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management • Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses) • Device is FDA approved Total ankle arthroplasty may also be indicated for revision of failed previous reconstructions where sufficient bone stock and soft tissue integrity are present.
21 Revision Total Ankle Arthroplasty Revision total ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met:
If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented.

Conservative management offered by the provider or other health professionals for this condition(s) should include footwear modification and/or padding/accommodative devices (e.g., foot orthosis) AND at least one of the following complementary strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and improve function:

• Activity modification • Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics • Corticosteroid injection(s) • Debridement of associated hyperkeratotic lesions, such as corns or calluses Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate.
If conservative management is not appropriate, the medical record must clearly document why such an approa ch is not reasonable.

For the purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes.
Adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery is strongly recommended.

Where there are patient-specific modifiable comorbidities that may adversely impact patient reported outcomes or the health status of the patient a shared decision-making process with the patient to discuss these modifiable comorbidities is strongly recommended and should be documented.
